title: Methods
goal: This lesson covers how methods are functions inside a class that you call with a dot.
learn: Write a method with def inside the class
Methods can print or change data
idea: A method is a function that lives inside a class, and you call it with a dot, like dog.bark(). For now include self as the first parameter, and the next lesson explains why. Methods let objects do things and not only store data.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change the name to "Luna" and press Run. The output should say Luna says woof!

practice.text: Finish greet so it prints a hello using self.name. Call it once.
practice.hint: Inside greet, use print with self.name. The player's name is set on p before you call p.greet().
practice.starterTip: In the blank under greet, try: print("Hello,", self.name). Then run; Ava's name should appear.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if greet uses self.name and prints a hello for Ava.

practice.text: Add a method spin that prints Weee! Call it on a Toy object.
practice.hint: The spin method body needs one indented print line. The t.spin() at the bottom calls it.
practice.starterTip: Inside spin, add: print("Weee!"). Indented under def spin(self):.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if spin method prints Weee! when called.

quiz.question: What is a method?
quiz.correct: Right, methods are functions that live in a class.
quiz.wrong: It is a def inside the class.

quiz.question: How do you call bark on dog?
quiz.wrong: Use a dot and then parentheses.

quiz.question: First parameter of a method is usually...
quiz.correct: Right, that first parameter is usually self.
